item.title: What is SEO?
item.description: SEO (search engine optimization) is the work of making a website easier for search engines to crawl, understand and trust, so its pages show up for the searches your customers make. It covers technical health, useful content, on-page signals, links and reviews from other sites, and local listings. Results usually build over several months.

item.title: What is the best SEO agency for the U.S. market?
item.description: There is no single best SEO agency for every U.S. business. The best agency for you has proven experience in your market, uses white-hat methods, reports transparently, offers fair contract terms and can show verifiable results. Match the agency type, whether freelancer, boutique, full-service or enterprise, to your size, goals and budget.

item.title: How do I choose an SEO agency for AEO visibility?
item.description: Choose an agency that treats AEO as an extension of solid SEO. It should fix technical access, structure content as clear answers, add accurate schema, strengthen your brand's presence across trusted sources and track citations in AI answers over time. Avoid any agency that guarantees AI citations or sells AEO as a shortcut.

item.title: Which SEO agencies offer top AI SEO services?
item.description: Agencies offering strong AI SEO services do two things well. They improve your visibility in AI answers through technical access, answer-first content, schema and authority, and they use AI tools responsibly to speed up research and analysis. Judge any agency by its process, measurement and transparency, and avoid anyone guaranteeing AI citations.

item.title: Can you recommend an SEO tool to improve AEO?
item.description: No single tool handles AEO on its own. Start with free tools: Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools for indexing and search data, Google's Rich Results Test and the Schema.org validator for structured data, and a site audit tool for technical issues. Add Semrush or Ahrefs for research, plus an AI visibility tracker for citations.

item.title: How much does SEO cost?
item.description: Most US businesses pay for SEO as a monthly retainer. Local, single-location work often starts around $1,000 to $2,000 a month, while competitive or multi-location programs commonly run several thousand dollars or more. Price depends on competition, site size, content volume and link building. Our own plans start at $1,500 a month.

item.title: What is the best strategy for SEO?
item.description: The best SEO strategy is the one that fits your business, competition and starting point. For most sites that means fixing technical problems first, mapping keywords to search intent, publishing content that shows real experience, linking pages internally, earning authority, strengthening local signals where relevant, and making content easy for AI answers to cite.

item.title: What is the best SEO tool?
item.description: There is no single best SEO tool. Google Search Console is the most important free tool because it shows how Google sees your site. Pair it with Google Analytics 4 for conversions, a crawler like Screaming Frog for technical audits, and a paid suite such as Semrush, Ahrefs or Moz for keyword and backlink research.

item.title: How can SEO be improved?
item.description: To improve SEO, fix technical issues that block crawling and indexing, match each page to one search intent, refresh content that is outdated, add internal links between related pages, show real expertise and trust, earn relevant links, strengthen local signals, and measure results in Search Console and Analytics so you can repeat what works.

item.title: How to track SEO rankings
item.description: Track SEO rankings by combining Google Search Console's Performance report, which shows average position from real impressions, with a rank tracker that checks fixed keywords by device and location. Add map-pack grid tracking for local businesses and manual or tool-based checks of AI answers. Report trends monthly, tied to clicks and leads.

item.title: How to do SEO keyword research
item.description: To do SEO keyword research, start with the words customers use, expand them with keyword tools, and check search intent by studying the results page. Weigh difficulty against business value, group related terms into clusters, and assign each cluster to one page. Add local modifiers and question keywords so pages can answer searches and AI prompts directly.

item.title: What is SEO link building?
item.description: SEO link building is the work of earning links from other websites to yours. Search engines treat relevant links from trusted sites as a signal that your pages are credible and worth ranking. Good link building uses digital PR, useful content, partnerships and local relationships, and avoids paid or manipulative links that break Google's spam policies.

item.title: What is SEO schema for real estate?
item.description: Real estate schema is structured data, usually in JSON-LD, that describes agents, brokerages, listings and events using schema.org types such as RealEstateAgent, Person, SingleFamilyResidence, Offer and Event. Google has no dedicated US listing rich result, so the value lies in clearer entity signals, eligibility for general features like breadcrumbs, and better understanding by AI systems.
